description: Found by defk-9p6.12 (examples/ws_masking.exs). A kernel that implements a behaviour callback (Bandit.PrimitiveOps.WebSocket.ws_mask/2) cannot carry @impl true: written before the defk, the attribute attaches to the first function the macro generates, __defk_load__/0, and Elixir warns 'got @impl true for __defk_load__/0 but no behaviour specifies such callback'. The kernel still satisfies the behaviour, so the example leaves @impl out (noted in its header). Done when @impl (true or a behaviour module) before a defk applies to the kernel's public function and the generated helpers carry none, with a test that a behaviour-implementing kernel compiles without warnings under --warnings-as-errors.
title: @impl true before a defk attaches to __defk_load__/0, not the kernel
